upstreamDeclaredFixes.summary: Invalidate fallback proofs after account linking.
Apply client ACR requirements to device authorization.
Preserve logout revocation settings during client registration updates.
Correct login-page HTML sanitization.
Correct bundled Brotli decoder memory safety.
Discard stale authentication state during organization login.
Harden SAML request processing against denial of service.
Validate logout hints against the intended session.
Bound SAML key-information parsing work.
Bound SAML authority parsing memory usage.
Protect session claims from client-registration mapper substitution.
Validate CIBA subject parameters before issuing tokens.
Enforce resource ownership in UMA permission requests.
Protect token principals from delegated client-manager changes.
Prevent attribute mappers from fabricating realm roles.
Preserve group permission denials during group moves.
Enforce expiration limits on exchanged tokens.
Protect resource-role claims from JSON mapper injection.
Restrict default-role changes by client creators.
Protect reserved subject and audience claims from mappers.
Close the authentication account-takeover race.
Require verified identity-provider email before automatic account linking.
Prevent identity rebinding after client recreation.
Bound XML processing at SAML resolution endpoints.
Apply delegated role permissions to composite roles.
Require proof for SAML holder-of-key assertions.
Honor SAML proxy restrictions during identity brokering.
Enforce audience validation for administrative API tokens.
Validate encoded SAML redirect parameter signatures.

excludedUpstreamClaims.reason: The upstream description is limited to Keycloak 26.8.0 and earlier; the previous published baseline is 26.8.1.
Standalone SAML-adapter compatibility is outside the image contract.
Administrative CLI scripts are removed from these runtime images.
The upstream fix concerns MySQL/MariaDB deployment modes; these profiles are optimized and validated for PostgreSQL.

distributionAudit.limits: The official archive is supplementary provenance. Native OCI builds independently enforce distribution JAR checksums; vulnerability-specific exploitation and live cloud databases are not tested.

limits: Fix inclusion is established from the official 26.8.2 security release and validated image inventories. Scanner absence is not local exploit reproduction.
Feature-dependent upstream fixes do not establish compatibility for untested extensions, identity-provider combinations or cloud databases.
Remaining findings, including unfixed HIGH OS advisories and four MariaDB JDBC advisories, are retained without suppression.
Counts from older scans use different database snapshots and are not measured repair deltas.
The original complete source reports remain in CI artifacts subject to retention; their SHA-256 hashes, database metadata and compact findings are retained here.
